title: A one-standard-deviation mean bound leaves 117 of 130 selected Allen independent-noise input sums unresolved
abstract: We tested the mean assumption in a model of convergent cortical inputs. Allen Synaptic Physiology r2.1 gave 130 selected same-sign input groups in mouse VisP and human TCx. Assigning medians as means reproduced 55 independent-noise sum losses against the best input. We derived exact gain bounds when each nonnegative mean differs from its median by at most k response standard deviations, with standard deviations fixed. At k=1, four losses and nine benefits held for all means; 117 groups were unresolved. At k=0.25, 53 groups were unresolved. Corner tests and linear programs agreed within 2.3e-15 across 1915 cases. The box is a relaxation, not a confidence interval or a measured mean shift. Independent noise, common signals, fixed noise scales and sign-preserving means are assumptions. The result does not establish a biological coding effect. Code, proof, aggregate evidence and external retrieval steps support reproduction; external record tables are excluded.

display.caption: Exact loss and benefit certificates under bounded mean shifts in selected independent-noise input-sum models.
